location_name: Indonesian EEZ (ZEE) off West Kalimantan / Natuna, South China Sea

reasoning: Seizure of a rival claimant's fishing vessels in Indonesia's claimed EEZ in the southern South China Sea is physical enforcement against Vietnam; coercive. The capture date is not given (the boats were still 100 miles out on 14 April), so month precision.

reasoning: A named multi-ship naval patrol on combat alert in the Natuna area to guard Indonesian waters against foreign (chiefly Vietnamese, Thai, Chinese, Malaysian) fishing is unilateral presence without confrontation; demonstrative. location_name: South China Sea (nine-dotted-lines map)
summary: Indonesia's Permanent Mission to the UN sent note verbale No. 480/POL-703/VII/10 to the UN Secretary-General, responding to China's 7 May 2009 note CML/17/2009 and its map, stating that remote or very small features in the South China Sea do not deserve an EEZ or continental shelf of their own and that the so-called 'nine-dotted-lines map' clearly lacks international legal basis and is tantamount to upsetting UNCLOS 1982, and asked that it be circulated to all UN members.
actors: Permanent Mission of the Republic of Indonesia to the United Nations; Ministry of Foreign Affairs
reasoning: A formal UN note verbale rejecting the legal basis of China's nine-dash line is a verbal/legal assertion of Indonesia's position; declarative. It is Indonesia's first formal written challenge to the line. The DOALOS listing (HTML) gives the date; the note itself is a scanned PDF (text read by OCR, not machine-checkable).
